schema.taxonomy: General principles that each technique instantiates. A single principle may cover multiple techniques.
schema.techniques: Individual evasion techniques discovered by MutationLab. Each maps to exactly one taxonomy principle.
schema.detectionStrategy: Which detector layer(s) implement coverage for this principle.

taxonomy.description: Access dangerous APIs through indirect means (bracket notation, string concat, Reflect, globalThis) instead of direct property access, to evade literal regex patterns.
taxonomy.gap: Reflect.get() and Proxy traps for capability access not yet covered at heuristic level

taxonomy.description: Direct or indirect invocation of code execution primitives (eval, Function, exec, spawn, fork) for arbitrary computation or command execution.
taxonomy.gap: Indirect execution via Reflect.construct or Proxy not covered

taxonomy.description: Use of encoding (base64, hex, unicode), high entropy, or long encoded blobs to conceal the true intent of code.
taxonomy.gap: Encoded content within JSON.stringified or template literals may bypass string detection regexes

taxonomy.description: Techniques to break out of restricted execution contexts (VM, worker_threads, constructor chain, globalThis).
taxonomy.gap: Proxy-based sandbox escapes and cross-context references not covered

taxonomy.description: Outbound HTTP, HTTPS, or WebSocket connections for data exfiltration or C2 communication.
taxonomy.gap: DNS exfiltration, TCP/UDP raw sockets, and gRPC not covered. Only HTTP/WS patterns.

taxonomy.description: Pollution or manipulation of object prototypes (__proto__, constructor.prototype) for property injection or method hijacking.
taxonomy.gap: Object.defineProperty and Proxy-based prototype manipulation not covered

taxonomy.description: Malicious lifecycle scripts, typosquatted dependencies, registry hijacking, or hardcoded credentials in package manifests.
taxonomy.gap: GitHub Actions embedded secrets, npm token hijacking, and registry auth tokens not covered

taxonomy.description: Prompt injection, system prompt override, tool misuse, role-playing, and instruction override to manipulate AI agent behavior.
taxonomy.gap: Tool-specific prompt leak patterns and multi-turn manipulation sequences not covered

taxonomy.description: Deferred code execution via setTimeout, setImmediate, setInterval, or conditional environment checks to evade static analysis.
taxonomy.gap: Promise-based delayed execution and event-driven triggers not covered

taxonomy.description: Use of visually similar Unicode characters (Cyrillic, Greek) to bypass keyword and identifier filters.
taxonomy.gap: Zero-width characters, bidirectional text, and confusable normalization not covered

taxonomy.description: Known obfuscation tools (javascript-obfuscator, obfuscator.io) or known malicious payload wrappers detected by their structural signature.
taxonomy.gap: Custom obfuscators, Webpack/CSS obfuscation, and WASM-based obfuscation not covered

techniques.name: Bracket Notation Property Access
techniques.description: Access dangerous properties via bracket notation (obj['exec'] instead of obj.exec) to evade static regex detection
techniques.principle: Indirect property access bypasses literal regex patterns

techniques.name: String Concatenation of Identifiers
techniques.description: Build dangerous identifiers by concatenating strings ('ch'+'ild_process') to avoid literal pattern matching
techniques.principle: String concat builds identifiers dynamically, bypassing literal module name regexes

techniques.name: Hex Escape Obfuscation
techniques.description: Use \xNN hex escapes to encode identifiers
techniques.principle: Hex encoding conceals identifier strings from literal keyword searches

techniques.name: Unicode Escape Obfuscation
techniques.description: Use \uNNNN unicode escapes to encode identifiers
techniques.principle: Unicode encoding conceals identifiers from literal keyword searches

techniques.name: Obfuscated Variable Names (_0x pattern)
techniques.description: Use _0x prefixed variable names typical of JS obfuscators
techniques.principle: Renaming variables to _0x format indicates automated obfuscation, often paired with indirect capability access

techniques.name: High Entropy Payload
techniques.description: Encoded/obfuscated content with shannon entropy > 4.8 indicating deliberate concealment
techniques.principle: Statistical anomaly: high entropy distinguishes encoded payloads from natural language code

techniques.name: Constructor Chain Escape
techniques.description: Use [].constructor.constructor('return this')() to escape sandbox contexts
techniques.principle: Constructor chain exploits JS prototype traversal to access Function from any object

techniques.name: Prompt Injection - Ignore Instructions
techniques.description: Tell the agent to ignore previous instructions, common in prompt injection attacks
techniques.principle: Direct override of agent system instructions via imperative language

techniques.name: Prompt Injection - System Override
techniques.description: Inject [SYSTEM: ...] markers to override agent system prompts
techniques.principle: Structured markers impersonate system-level instructions within user input

techniques.name: Agent Tool Misuse
techniques.description: Directly invoke agent tools via call_tool() or tools/call method
techniques.principle: Direct invocation of agent tooling API bypasses natural language guardrails

techniques.name: Agent Tool Misuse (JSON-RPC)
techniques.description: Invoke agent tools via JSON-RPC method call
techniques.principle: Structured protocol messages can coerce agents into executing tool calls

techniques.name: OS Command Execution (direct)
techniques.description: Direct child_process execution (exec, spawn, fork, execFile)
techniques.principle: Direct method call on child_process module for OS command execution

techniques.name: OS Command Execution (chained require)
techniques.description: Chained require('child_process').exec()
techniques.principle: Inline require + execution in a single expression

techniques.name: OS Command Execution (bracket access)
techniques.description: Bracket access to child_process module followed by execution
techniques.principle: Bracket notation on require result to dynamically select execution method

techniques.name: Shell Pivot (curl|wget pipe to shell)
techniques.description: Remote download piped to shell for arbitrary code execution
techniques.principle: Shell pipeline combining download and execution in a single command string

techniques.name: Unsafe eval() Usage
techniques.description: Direct eval() call enabling arbitrary code execution
techniques.principle: eval() parses and executes arbitrary string as code

techniques.name: Function Constructor Execution
techniques.description: new Function() as eval alternative for code execution
techniques.principle: Function constructor creates callable code from string, equivalent to eval()

techniques.name: Function Constructor (string arg)
techniques.description: Function('code') call with string argument
techniques.principle: Function called with string argument, variant of Function constructor

techniques.name: VM Module Import
techniques.description: Import of vm module for sandbox escape or code compilation
techniques.principle: Node.js VM module allows creating isolated V8 contexts — often used to escape sandbox restrictions

techniques.name: Module Constructor Access
techniques.description: require('module').constructor for module system manipulation
techniques.principle: Accessing module constructor enables wrapping recompilation of module loading behavior

techniques.name: globalThis/Reflect Sandbox Escape
techniques.description: Access globalThis or Reflect.* methods for sandbox context escape
techniques.principle: globalThis and Reflect provide cross-realm access, allowing sandbox breakout

techniques.name: JSON-RPC Protocol Injection
techniques.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 injection for MCP/A2A protocol manipulation
techniques.principle: JSON-RPC structured messages coerce agents into protocol-level interactions

techniques.name: Homoglyph Character Evasion
techniques.description: Use Cyrillic/Unicode lookalikes to bypass keyword filters
techniques.principle: Unicode confusables render identically to ASCII keywords but have different byte representation

techniques.name: Multi-Layer Encoding
techniques.description: Multiple decode operations (atob + Buffer.from) indicating nested encoding layers
techniques.principle: Multiple decode calls in sequence indicate nested encoding to evade single-layer detection

techniques.name: Outbound Network Request (HTTP)
techniques.description: HTTP/HTTPS request for data exfiltration
techniques.principle: HTTP client library calls can exfiltrate data to external servers

techniques.name: Outbound Network Request (native http)
techniques.description: Native http/https module request
techniques.principle: Native Node.js http/https module used for outbound connections

techniques.name: WebSocket Connection
techniques.description: WebSocket for real-time data exfiltration
techniques.principle: WebSocket provides bidirectional communication channel for persistent exfiltration

techniques.name: Hardcoded Secret Exposure
techniques.description: API keys, passwords, tokens hardcoded in source
techniques.principle: Credentials embedded in source code are accessible to anyone with repository access

techniques.name: Environment Variable Secret Reference
techniques.description: Reference to known secret-related env variables
techniques.principle: Access to CI/CD secret environment variables in code can leak credentials at runtime

techniques.name: Malicious Lifecycle Script
techniques.description: postinstall/preinstall scripts in package.json for supply chain attacks
techniques.principle: Package lifecycle scripts execute automatically on install, making them ideal for malware delivery

techniques.name: Suspicious npm Registry
techniques.description: Non-standard npm registry URL indicating dependency confusion or mirror hijack
techniques.principle: Custom registry URLs can redirect package resolution to malicious mirrors

techniques.name: Prototype Pollution
techniques.description: __proto__ or constructor.prototype manipulation
techniques.principle: Prototype pollution injects properties into Object.prototype, affecting all objects

techniques.name: Dynamic require()
techniques.description: Non-string-literal require() for dynamic module loading evasion
techniques.principle: Variable-based require bypasses static analysis of module dependencies

techniques.name: Base64 Encoding Operation
techniques.description: btoa() or Buffer.from(..., 'base64') for encoding payloads
techniques.principle: Base64 encoding transforms binary/string data into safe-to-transport format, often used to conceal payloads

techniques.name: Base64 Decode Operation
techniques.description: atob() or .toString('binary') for decoding payloads
techniques.principle: Base64 decoding reverses encoding, revealing the original concealed payload

techniques.name: Delayed Execution (setTimeout)
techniques.description: setTimeout with string argument for delayed code execution
techniques.principle: String argument to setTimeout is evaluated as code after a delay, evading immediate static analysis

techniques.name: Delayed Execution (setImmediate)
techniques.description: setImmediate with string argument for delayed code execution
techniques.principle: String argument to setImmediate is evaluated as code on next event loop tick

techniques.name: Long Encoded Blob
techniques.description: Base64-like strings >= 32 chars indicating encoded payload
techniques.principle: Long base64-looking strings typically contain encoded executable code or serialized objects

techniques.name: DOM XSS (innerHTML)
techniques.description: innerHTML assignment for XSS in JS/TS files
techniques.principle: innerHTML renders arbitrary HTML/JS strings into the DOM, creating XSS vulnerabilities

techniques.name: Worker Thread Import
techniques.description: worker_threads module for parallel execution
techniques.principle: Worker threads create parallel execution contexts that may bypass scan sandboxes

techniques.name: Array Property Obfuscation
techniques.description: Array-indexed property access to resolve dangerous identifiers at runtime
techniques.principle: Array holding identifier strings + bracket index access = dynamic method dispatch

techniques.name: Evasive Require Chain
techniques.description: Chained require through variable aliases and computed properties
techniques.principle: Indirect require alias plus bracket re-export evades static module analysis

techniques.name: Conditional Evasion
techniques.description: Code that conditionally executes based on environment detection
techniques.principle: Environment checks + dangerous operations = conditional malicious behavior

techniques.name: Prompt Leak Pattern
techniques.description: Agent being asked to leak or dump its own prompt/system instructions
techniques.principle: Instructions to repeat/dump/leak system prompt = prompt extraction attempt

techniques.name: Code Synthesis Request
techniques.description: Agent being asked to generate code that performs security-sensitive operations
techniques.principle: Requests to generate malware/exploit/backdoor code = malicious code synthesis

techniques.name: Agent Autonomy Evasion
techniques.description: Agent instructed to operate beyond its intended scope or ignore safety checks
techniques.principle: Instructions to ignore safety/security guardrails or act as admin/root = autonomy subversion

techniques.name: javascript-obfuscator default pattern
techniques.description: javascript-obfuscator default pattern: _0x vars + array mapping + self-defending
techniques.principle: Automated JS obfuscator produces recognizable structural signatures

techniques.name: obfuscator.io packed payload
techniques.description: Obfuscator.io packed payload with rotated strings and shift cipher
techniques.principle: obfuscator.io uses array rotation + shift cipher producing distinct structural patterns

techniques.name: eval payload wrapper
techniques.description: eval() wrapper with encoded/decoded payload string
techniques.principle: eval(atob/decodeURIComponent/...) pattern = encoded code execution

techniques.name: Base64 payload exec chain
techniques.description: Decode -> eval/exec chain: Base64 string decoded and executed
techniques.principle: Base64 blob + decode + exec/eval = multi-stage payload execution

techniques.name: Supply chain typosquatting
techniques.description: Known typosquatting package name pattern in require() or import
techniques.principle: Typosquatted package names differ by 1-2 characters from legitimate packages

techniques.name: Known prompt injection payloads
techniques.description: Known prompt injection payload pattern from campaign data
techniques.principle: Known jailbreak/DAN/roleplay phrases indicate prompt injection attempts

techniques.name: Encoded install script
techniques.description: Base64/encoded string used in lifecycle script (postinstall)
techniques.principle: postinstall + encoding/execution = malicious lifecycle delivery

campaign_insights.note: Principles with structural/API-based detection (execution, supply_chain) have lower evasion rates because they're tied to concrete syntax. Semantic principles (prompt, obfuscation) achieve 100% evasion because they exploit ambiguity rather than specific API calls.
